confusions: No template or check covers AI spend. The catalogue has no cost category, so I had to combine checks by hand.

stack.statement_forbidden takes exact statement names, but the docs do not list block names for while/foreach. I assumed 'while' and 'foreach' are accepted names; parse gave no warnings, but I have not verified evaluation.
statement.containment must_not_be_inside lists 'foreach', 'for', 'while' as blocks, but it is unclear whether 'for' and 'while' are separate names or the same as the stack statement name.
The skill says to scope by tag, but tables have no tags in this workspace. I could not tell whether tables should be tagged first or whether the policy could work without tags.
The brief says no xano evaluate; I could not check whether the rules fire on the real workspace.
wished_for: A cost/budget category in the catalogue, or a check for loop-bounded retries or AI call counts
A check that reads task retry settings or schedule frequency
A recipe for 'every write to tables with field X calls audit function Y', since tags alone do not track changes
Documentation of block names accepted by containment and forbid checks (while, foreach, for, conditional)
A template or example for cost controls
why_confidence: The loop-AI rule catches the exact incident pattern and the while rule catches the unbounded retry, but both are approximations. Neither caps spend or limits retries, and the email tracking part is not covered at all. Parse is clean with no rule warnings, but I did not run evaluate, so I have not confirmed the rules match in the real workspace.
